item.title: Version 3.0.0
item.description:
CedarLogic v3.0.0 is the largest release the project has had in quite a while. There is a brand new renderer, a new circuit file format, and a long list of fixes to many many different parts of the app.

Everything draws through Skia now

The fixed-function OpenGL renderer is gone and replaced with Skia! Gates, wires, text, the minimap, the oscilloscope, and the gate palette all render through [Skia](https://skia.org), the same 2D engine behind Chrome.

Curved gate bodies are now actually curved, text stays sharp instead of getting blurry as you zoom in, and the gate thumbnails in the palette are anti-aliased.

Panning is a replay of a cached scene instead of a full redraw, so dragging around a large circuit is much smoother now.

Vector export is now a first class citizen with much less hackery then before.

A new circuit format

Saved circuits use a new S-expression `.cdl` format (v3) inspired by KiCAD. It is designed to be human readable, is lossless about wire routing (contains the whole segment tree now instead of a flattened polyline), and is more easier to build a parser for.

v1 and v2 files are still able to load, with a migration notice for breaking changes. Conversion to v3 is opt-in per file and CedarLogic not silently overwrite an older version without explicit confirmation.

There are still export options for the v1 and v2 xml file formats.

Undo and redo

Undo and redo now jump to the page the command was made on, including adding and deleting tabs, and parameter-dialog edits land on the proper page now. Redo after a paste no longer crashes on a freed gate.

The edit menu's keyboard shortcuts were also adjusted: adding Ctrl+Shift+Z as an additional redo hotkey and adding Cut!

Atomicity

The Autosave system was rewritten. Saves are now atomic, so a crash mid-write can no longer truncate a circuit, and the autosave now runs on the GUI thread against a snapshot preventing simulation races.

There is a proper lock on files as well preventing two conflicting Cedarlogic sessions.

Crash logs and stack traces!

A crash now writes a symbolized stack trace and opens a pre-filled GitHub issue, with the report copied to your clipboard as well. Windows catches unhandled exceptions; macOS and Linux catch fatal signals. If CedarLogic goes down without a dialog it will also let you know the next time you start the program.

Interface

The menu bar is reorganized to better fit where applications place their items nowadays.

The toolbar sports a new set of SVG icons on Windows and Linux.

Gate thumbnails in the palette are bigger, fill the column width, and are properly centered in their tiles.

Rotation is now clockwise, which is the direction everyone expected it to go.

On macOS the palette scrollbar is now readable in dark mode.

Fixes

  • The simulation keeps a steady cadence while the GUI is busy.
  • The palette scrollbar no longer overlaps the gates, and scrolling is smoother.
  • DECODER produced the wrong number of outputs; it is now 2^n.
  • Starting with an empty gate library no longer crashes.
  • Quitting exits cleanly instead of hanging in framework teardown.
  • Status bar white-line artifacts are gone in both light and dark mode.
  • Gates no longer vanish on pages opened before the first paint.
  • Moving a wire whose gate has gone missing no longer inserts phantom gates.
  • The Windows build links the WinSparkle library matching its architecture, so auto-update works on the 32-bit build.
  • Fonts come from fontconfig on Linux rather than a scan of the working directory, so the app draws text wherever you launched it from.
  • Glyph outlines are built at a fixed reference size, so text does not shift as you zoom.

Under the hood

`MainApp`'s globals are now proper services (settings, gate library, and the GUI/logic bridge). Gates come from a registry with a typed parameter schema instead of a giant if-else megacase and the logic thread wakes on a condition variable rather than polling every millisecond. Collision checks run through a spatial grid. There is a wire-router seam with its own trunk router and tests, headless `--render` modes for golden-image testing, and a proper CI test suite (doctest, CTest, CMake presets) covering a subset of gates. The half-finished `simulator/` rewrite is retired.

Skia is now a required dependency, pinned to a milestone and built and cached per platform in CI, with `task skia:download` to fetch a prebuilt one. There is a `Taskfile.yaml` and a Nix devshell, so `task build`, `task test`, and `task release` do the obvious things. See

[Building](https://github.com/taciturnaxolotl/CedarLogic/blob/master/docs/Building.md).

Full Changelog: https://github.com/taciturnaxolotl/CedarLogic/compare/v2.4.3...v3.0.0
